summary: Queries an open file slot (index a1, guarded by the open-file count uNumber and the slot in-use flag) and fills a caller result buffer with the file's type, size and timestamp information. Disk files (GetFileType 1) take the full GetFileInformationByHandle path with per-time FILETIME-to-systemtime conversion and a compressed datetime via sub_591EDF; character devices (type 2) and pipes (type 3) get a minimal header plus an available-data count (PeekNamedPipe for pipes). Failures set the TLS error to 9 via TLSOffsetGetter, map GetLastError through ErrorIDLookupTable, and return -1.

operations.description: Validate slot a1: require a1 below the open-file count uNumber and the slot entry's in-use flag bit (byte at +4 of each 36-byte slot entry) set; otherwise fail immediately.
Enter the slot's critical section with CriticalSectionEnterWithLazyInit(a1) before any file query.
Query the slot handle's type with GetFileType, then clear the high byte of the returned type flags.
Branch on the file type: 1 takes the disk-file path; 2 (character device) and 3 (pipe) initialize the character-device buffer; 0 and unknown types take the failure path.

For a character device or pipe, write the result buffer header: block size word at +6 (0x2000 for a character device, 4096 for a pipe), flags word +8 set to 1, slot id stored at +0 and +16, zero words at +4, +12 and +10, and zero dwords at +24, +28 and +32.
Set the available-data dword at +20: forced to 0 for character devices, else the value from PeekNamedPipe (also 0 when PeekNamedPipe fails).
Disk-file path: retrieve attributes, sizes and timestamps with GetFileInformationByHandle into a local BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION; failure goes to the error path.
Encode the attribute/permission bits into the +6 word of the buffer: OR 0x124 when the read-only attribute is set, otherwise OR 0x1B6.
Convert the last-write FILETIME to local time with FileTimeToLocalFileTime and then to system time with FileTimeToSystemTime; failure aborts to the error path.
Pack the last-write date/time into the compressed form with sub_591EDF(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, -1) and store it at +28 of the buffer.
Convert the last-access FILETIME when non-zero and store it at +24; when the creation time is zero, reuse the last-write value for the creation slot and mark the +7 high bit.
Complete the disk entry: copy the file size low dword into +20, set +16 and +0 to 0, write the creation value at +32 and OR 0x80 into the byte at +7 when creation equals last-write.
Error path: read GetLastError and map it through ErrorIDLookupTable before failing.
Write the TLS error value 9 via TLSOffsetGetter and return -1 when the slot is invalid or a query step fails.
Leave the slot's critical section with FileCriticalSectionLeave(a1) on every exit from the queried path.

clean_pseudocode: *(int *)(out + 28) = sub_591EDF(st.wYear, st.wMonth, st.wDay, st.wHour, st.wMinute, st.wSecond, -1);
*(int *)(out + 24) = sub_591EDF(st.wYear, st.wMonth, st.wDay, st.wHour, st.wMinute, st.wSecond, -1);
created = sub_591EDF(st.wYear, st.wMonth, st.wDay, st.wHour, st.wMinute, st.wSecond, -1);
unresolved: The array base dword_8D4920 for the 36-byte open-file slot entries has no packet global reference; the slot-array indexing in the description is derived from the decompiled expression a1 >> 5 / a1 & 31.

The exact meaning of the buffer word at +6 differs by file type (block size for devices, attribute/permission bits for disk files); the disk-file attribute masks 0x124/0x1B6 are taken from the raw source.
The TLS value 9 written on failure is a known error id but its message table entry is not resolved here.
